Why do we talk about climate change more than we talk about pollution these days? CO2 levels have been higher in the past, and the biosphere was booming. I'm more worried about novel chemicals.

Ya know, artificial hormones and nerve-disruptor pesticides, and the other tens of thousands of manufactured chemicals that this planet has never had to deal with before WWII, might be worse than fucking plant food.

"fucking plant food" is actually one of the most severe pollutants sheerly because of the huge, HUGE amounts that get dumped into the water. Fertilizer induces algae blooms, which produce a lot of oxygen at first, but then as the algae dies and decays it actually uses up more O2 than it produces, resulting in a completely de-oxygenated area of water in which fish suffocate because there's nothing there for them to breathe. It's called hypoxia. I'm sure if we dumped any of those other chemicals in the water at the same rates, they would have even worse effects, but we're just not.

On the other hand, I'm glad to see some other folks with reservations about novel chemicals. A lot of my friends repeat the line "everything is chemicals" so much that I really don't think they see a distinction between naturally-occurring molecules and synthetics. I think we need to popularize a word to differentiate between the two.

Eh. I am already quite worried about climate change, because my poor country is dealing with it right now.

You know what isn't normal? Having 2-3 bad flood events in a 4 month period, instead of the once every 5-10 years we are prepared for. Or the fact that it's snowing waaaay before they expected in our alpine regions. Or the massive cyclones that were constantly slamming into our tropics all summer.

I get it. It's not a sexy topic, and there is still 'controversy', but the fact is there are places right now that are dealing with these effects right now. Hell, we would probably be a lot better off and handle it well if we had proper resource management, but we don't.

In my current homebrew world, there was this big old age of prosperity, where the region where most of the game play takes place is at peace, and all is good. Great wonders have been built, and everyone is happy. In the center of all of this is this massive empire, which has expanded over the region and subjugated many a people. Now, the world at large is polytheistic, but there are parthenons and churches that are fairly widespread. This empire is the center of worship for the god of peace, prosperity, love, etc etc. There is a prophecy that states that he will send a prophet to the world to lead it to a great age of peace and happiness, greater than the one they currently experience.

The god, happy with his followers, goes to the gods of life, souls, and automatons, and find a way to incarnate his soul into a mortal, leaving behind his godly knowledge and much of his power, but retaining his will and general directions. Unfortunately, the great empire he had been born to is poisoned by its decadence, and corruption has rotted it to its core. The church and the emperor, fearing the loss of the power they held, seek out the prophet (who, despite the visions and power he wields, has no idea what he is) and torture and execute him. When the god wakes back up, he is wracked by the betrayal and pain of what happened to him.

He loses it with grief. He casts off his former titles, and becomes the god of pain, hatred, and suffering, patron to the downtrodden. The empire begins a slow collapse as the blessings and guidance of the god disappears. The corruption worsens. The god guides a champion, a revolutionary, who leads a great army. The people rebel, and a great war wages that results in the champion becoming a martyr and the empire being dissolved, as the formerly reconquered secede. The army, who now worship this new god, stamp out the remnants of this former religion, executing clergy and destroying holy texts and records. A lot of knowledge about this time is lost, because so many records were destroyed in the process. The rebellion ends, and the army dissolves.

As things calm down, the former emperor, who manages to escape the collapse of the empire, makes a deal with the Mad God, (not the same god as before) to regain his throne. The Mad God, who seeks to use him as a pawn against the other gods, empowers the emperor, who builds up another army to reconquer the continent. Deals are made, and the Mad God strongarms the armies of hell to join the war. So the emperor manages to build up and gather legions of general ne'er-do-wells, like liches and other typically frowned upon entities, and wages a massive war to conquer the known world. The Mad God also uses him to wipe out centers of power for the other gods, seeking to stamp out their worship. Over the course of about forty years, the Mad God and the emperor are eventually beaten back. However, this involved an unprecedented degree of interference by the other gods, and it shows. Great weapons of war were created in the conflict, and the continent bears the markings. The kingdoms that once reigned in the Age of Gold collapsed in the chaos, and an age of darkness descends, with no true authority of any sort in the land. Millions die in both the war and the aftermath, and the continent basically rebuilds. This opens up tons of adventure with old artefacts and ruins scattered across the land for the party, who comes along over a thousand years afterwards, to explore in.

The best thing you can do is get a small blacklight. Any time you go to a thrift store, garage sale, antique store, just light things up and see what glows. After a while you'll get an idea of what it looks like, and that is when the fun begins. It will happen often that you will find something that is UG when you are certain it's not, or vice-versa. It's like hunting without the carnage. It's an adventure to find something cool that others just won't see. And, you will be collecting something that is radioactive!

You'll also notice that other things fluoresce as well. A real ruby will glow bright red under black light, but a fake one won't. Old transparent red glass marbles when hit with the blacklight will reveal swirls of fine dust inside (it's gold used to make the glass red).
